title: Your ETF Investments Just Got Safer: SEBI's New Price Rules
description: From today, September 7, 2026, SEBI has changed how Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) trade. The 'base price' for ETFs will now be based on yesterday's actual mark.

faq.a: An ETF (Exchange Traded Fund) is an investment fund that holds a basket of assets like stocks or bonds, and its units are traded on a stock exchange throughout the day, much like individual company shares.

faq.q: What does 'base price' mean for an ETF?
faq.a: The base price is a reference point used to calculate the maximum allowed price movement (price bands) for an ETF on a given trading day. Under the new rules, it's mostly based on the previous day's closing market price.
Price bands are limits set by the exchange that define the maximum percentage an ETF's price can move up or down from its base price in a single trading day.

A cooling-off period is a temporary pause of 15 minutes (or 5 minutes in the last half hour) that triggers when an ETF's price hits its initial dynamic price band, allowing investors time to react before the band can potentially expand further.

faq.q: When did these new rules come into effect?
faq.a: These new rules for ETF trading came into effect from today, September 7, 2026.
